figures.title: Lithium-ion charging and discharging
figures.alt: Original paired lithium-ion schematic with charger and load, separator, electrodes, lithium-ion paths and external electrical paths. See the adjacent source correction for current direction.
figures.caption: Extracted unchanged from the supplied handout. Electrode names follow the discharge convention; electrochemical anode/cathode roles reverse during charging.
figures.source_discrepancy: The charging panel puts “Current” and “Electron” labels on a shared dotted path. Do not read these as flows in the same direction: conventional current is opposite electron flow. During charging the external supply removes electrons from the positive electrode and delivers electrons to the negative electrode; Li⁺ moves through the electrolyte from positive to negative. During discharge, Li⁺ and electrons both move from negative to positive, through electrolyte and external load respectively. Use these directions and the written reactions when reproducing the source diagram.
